title: Get started with rthologs
text: Use orthologs() find orthologs set genes. Give genes, source species genes, target species. result standard data frame one row known ortholog input genes. target_ columns identify ortholog. source target can two species package.
code: odf <- orthologs("TP53", source = "human", target = "mouse") odf #>   input source_symbol target_symbol target_ncbi_id  target_ensembl_id #> 1  TP53          TP53         Trp53          22059 ENSMUSG00000059552 odf <- orthologs("Trp53", source = "mouse", target = "rat") odf #>   input source_symbol target_symbol target_ncbi_id  target_ensembl_id #> 1 Trp53         Trp53          Tp53          24842 ENSRNOG00000010756

title: Get started with rthologs
text: input can gene symbols, NCBI IDs, Ensembl IDs. Inputs case-sensitive can mix input types one vector. input direct match can match gene synonym. use primary names, set synonyms = FALSE.
code: genes <- c("TP53", "7157", "ENSG00000141510") odf <- orthologs(genes, source = "human", target = "mouse") odf #>             input source_symbol target_symbol target_ncbi_id  target_ensembl_id #> 1            TP53          TP53         Trp53          22059 ENSMUSG00000059552 #> 2            7157          TP53         Trp53          22059 ENSMUSG00000059552 #> 3 ENSG00000141510          TP53         Trp53          22059 ENSMUSG00000059552 genes <- c("GAPDH", "CTGF", "SEPT7") orthologs(genes, source = "human", target = "mouse") #>   input source_symbol target_symbol target_ncbi_id  target_ensembl_id #> 1 GAPDH         GAPDH         Gapdh          14433 ENSMUSG00000057666 #> 2  CTGF          CCN2          Ccn2          14219 ENSMUSG00000019997 #> 3 SEPT7       SEPTIN7       Septin7         235072 ENSMUSG00000001833 orthologs(genes, source = "human", target = "mouse", synonyms = FALSE) #>   input source_symbol target_symbol target_ncbi_id  target_ensembl_id #> 1 GAPDH         GAPDH         Gapdh          14433 ENSMUSG00000057666

title: Get started with rthologs
text: Set details = TRUE include source gene IDs supporting methods. support support_ncolumns list ortholog sources count.
code: odf <- orthologs("TP53", source = "human", target = "mouse", details = TRUE) dplyr::glimpse(odf) #> Rows: 1 #> Columns: 11 #> $ input             <chr> "TP53" #> $ source_taxon_id   <int> 9606 #> $ source_symbol     <chr> "TP53" #> $ source_ncbi_id    <chr> "7157" #> $ source_ensembl_id <chr> "ENSG00000141510" #> $ target_taxon_id   <int> 10090 #> $ target_symbol     <chr> "Trp53" #> $ target_ncbi_id    <chr> "22059" #> $ target_ensembl_id <chr> "ENSMUSG00000059552" #> $ support           <chr> "HGNC|Hieranoid|InParanoid|OMA|OrthoFinder|OrthoInsp… #> $ support_n         <int> 9

title: Get started with rthologs
text: input can one ortholog. ortholog gets row. default, result includes best matches. get potential orthologs, set best = FALSE. Set min_support keep pairs certain number supporting methods.
code: orthologs(genes = c("Ptprc", "Hba-a1", "Gapdh"), source = "mouse", target = "zebrafish") #>    input source_symbol target_symbol target_ncbi_id  target_ensembl_id #> 1  Ptprc         Ptprc         ptprc         559154 ENSDARG00000071437 #> 2 Hba-a1        Hba-a1       hbae1.1          30597 ENSDARG00000089475 #> 3 Hba-a1        Hba-a1         hbaa2         497166 ENSDARG00000069735 #> 4  Gapdh         Gapdh         gapdh         317743 ENSDARG00000043457 odf <- orthologs(   "Hba-a1",   source = "mouse",   target = "zebrafish",   best = FALSE,   details = TRUE ) odf[, c("input", "target_symbol", "support_n")] #>    input target_symbol support_n #> 1 Hba-a1       hbae1.1         8 #> 2 Hba-a1         hbaa2         8 #> 3 Hba-a1         hbae4         4 odf <- orthologs(   "Hba-a1",   source = "mouse",   target = "zebrafish",   best = FALSE,   min_support = 6,   details = TRUE ) odf[, c("input", "target_symbol", "support_n")] #>    input target_symbol support_n #> 1 Hba-a1       hbae1.1         8 #> 2 Hba-a1         hbaa2         8

title: Get started with rthologs
text: default, output includes genes known orthologs. keep inputs, set orthologs_only = FALSE. Genes without orthologs get one row NA columns. Cd34 valid mouse gene, data contain zebrafish ortholog . Fakegene mouse gene.

title: Gene Orthologs for Model Organisms
text: rthologs maps genes orthologs species. Supports common model organisms, including human, mouse, zebrafish, fly. Looks genes symbol, NCBI (Entrez) ID, Ensembl ID. Returns matches tidy R data frame can filter, summarize, join data. Works offline.

title: Find gene orthologs — orthologs
text: genes character vector gene symbols NCBI/Ensembl gene IDs (case-sensitive). source Species genes, "mouse". See species(). target Species find orthologs. synonyms TRUE (default), check synonyms input genes. best TRUE (default), keep best matches. min_support Minimum number sources support gene pair. orthologs_only TRUE (default), keep matching pairs. details TRUE, return source gene IDs support sources.

title: Find gene orthologs — orthologs
text: data frame one row per distinct input matching gene pair. columns input, source_symbol, target_symbol, target_ncbi_id, target_ensembl_id. details = TRUE, columns also include source_taxon_id, source_ncbi_id, source_ensembl_id, target_taxon_id, support (methods sources support pair), support_n (number ).

title: rthologs: Gene Orthologs for Model Organisms — rthologs-package
text: Genomic analysis frequently involves comparisons human mouse data. requires harmonization gene names gene space. 'rthologs' R package simplifies cross-species conversion mapping gene orthologs/homologs common model organisms human, mouse, rat, zebrafish, fly. supports gene symbols, NCBI (Entrez) IDs, Ensembl IDs, works offline. orthologs sourced Alliance Genome Resources (AGR) doi:10.1093/genetics/iyae049 .
